fixes.rationale_full: The test name was kept (no test-case removal) and both untested halves are now exercised. Lockout: user 'lo' has a real PBKDF2 hash. The right password gives SUCCESS, three wrong ones give INVALID_CREDENTIALS, and then the right password gives INVALID_CREDENTIALS (locked). This goes through auth.passwordLogin().attempt with a latch wait, the same helper AuthWave7KotlinTest uses. WebSocket wrapper: the app is started on an InMemoryHttpAdapter. An upgrade without a credential gets 401 and no handover. An upgrade with the Bearer access token opens a channel, and the wrapped handler sends auth.user(req).id (a deadline poll of 10 s, which the happy path does not wait for). The handshake is 101. The describe() assertion is kept (rule 2).
JDBC removed: the JdbcRefreshTokenStore tautology line no longer exists in AuthWave5KotlinTest (CON-IAM-003). The test checks only the in-memory and file stores.

fixes.rationale_full: Thread.sleep(10) is replaced by an event: ReachedLimit (a NoLimit subclass; NoLimit is no longer final) counts down a latch when the login reaches the user-only limit check (key 'login:u:'), the last step before the hash. The test awaits it (20 s) before sending /health. Right after /health returns it records !failing.isDone() and asserts it ('the failing login was still waiting when /health was answered'). Each exchange is timed from its own start (an AtomicLong set inside the pool task), so the kept healthAt < failedAt assertion compares real durations. The new assertion fails whenever the delayed 401 had already arrived before /health was answered.

fixes.why_no_red: Not applied: the requested change weakens an existing assertion (rule 2). Only the fixed sleep was replaced by a latch.
fixes.rationale_full: Partial, additive only. The fixed sleep max(20, floor/4) is replaced by an event (rule 3): the latch waits until as many failures as there are workers (2) have reached the hash step, with a 20 s deadline. A floor that held its worker would then hold every worker. pending > 0 stays the main signal. The requested relaxation of the bound (health.millis < floorMillis to < 0.5*50*floor/workers) was NOT applied, because rule 2 forbids weakening an assertion. The idle-probe-vs-loaded-latency bound and its residual CPU-contention flakiness stay as the reviewer described, and need a decision outside this fixer's rules.

fixes.rationale_full: Thread.sleep(200) is replaced by a bounded poll (10 s deadline; it exits as soon as the thread leaves NEW/RUNNABLE) on logoutAll.getState(). The test then asserts isAlive (the kept assertion), that the state is BLOCKED, WAITING or TIMED_WAITING, and that the stored tokenVersion is still 7 while the profile mutator holds the lock. A ver++ that takes no lock would end (TERMINATED) or write 8 before release, and the test now fails then even on a slow scheduler.
